approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a molecular autoencoder from unlabeled molecules, freezes it, and searches its 24-dimensional latent space with CMA-ES. It samples a Gaussian, deterministically decodes each point into a molecule, and evaluates valid new identities. Each accepted score stays attached to the exact point that generated that molecule. It collects two protocol batches into one scored generation, then uses the better samples to move the Gaussian mean, adapt its full covariance, and control its step size through cumulative paths. High-scoring initial molecules supply geometric starting locations, while subsequent adaptation uses scores of actual decoded offspring.
approach.novelty: Make each completed protocol batch a CMA generation, allowing the next batch to use the feedback that just arrived. This changes the delay between observation and distribution adaptation. The existing rank-weighted mean, covariance, and step-size equations automatically use the smaller generation. The lineage currently contains only its evaluated root, so batch-aligned adaptation has no earlier sibling experiment. The hypothesis is that more opportunities to redirect search within the same evaluation allowance can outweigh the noisier selection statistics of smaller generations.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-bd0cbfe35fa3 keeps its Gaussian fixed across two protocol batches. Its supplied screening replica completed 29 batches per objective but only 14 scored generations of 20 offspring. Direct joins of its cma_batch, cma_update, and cma_feedback receipts show that only 14 of 28 nonterminal feedback events advanced the Gaussian; the other 14 were followed by another batch sampled before that feedback. The last ten scored offspring remained a terminal partial generation. All rank, full-covariance, and step-size updates activated correctly, so the directly observed bottleneck is feedback waiting for another batch before it can affect proposals. Its macro score was 0.302617078892174, with task values ranging from 0.06351092410835005 to 0.6107459743674006. Those are one-replica observations, not a three-seed reliability estimate or proof that adaptation delay caused low scores. The Parent Curate observation explicitly identifies the short sequence of completed generations as a possible limitation; its broad geometry diagnostics leave the separate representation hypothesis unresolved.
hypothesis: Reduce the scored CMA generation target to the smallest whole number of evaluator-announced batches containing at least two offspring, so accepted feedback updates the inherited Gaussian after each complete protocol batch whenever that batch already contains at least two members.

finding_summary.headline: Immediate feedback updates activated, but the mean score fell by 0.0224
finding_summary.insights: Removing the measured feedback wait did not solve the score limitation in this replica. More updates also meant smaller selected populations: effective selection mass fell from 5.94 to 3.17, and average covariance movement per update decreased on every task. Thus update count is insufficient evidence of stronger or more useful adaptation. The docking trajectory makes the distinction concrete: 25 of its 29 generations contained tied scores, and one update had weighted score enrichment of only about 2.6 × 10⁻¹³ despite moving the Gaussian. The molecular assessment still finds oversized hydrocarbons, repeated imine or sulfur linkers, and elaborate carbonyl-bearing rings, with limited controlled variation of conventional scaffolds. Faster reaction to the available scores did not resolve those generator limitations. This supports investigating the representation and the informativeness of sampled regions alongside adaptation cadence. It does not establish which caused the score loss, whether the smaller selection mass increased harmful noise, or whether the result generalizes beyond the single paired seed.
finding_summary.results: Every completed batch immediately updated the Gaussian, and the next batch used that updated distribution. For each of the five tasks, accepted offspring waited through zero further batch emissions before their update, versus a mean of 0.5 emissions among updated Parent offspring. The Parent also left 10 accepted offspring per task in an unfinished terminal generation; the Child left none. Feedback changed the distribution used for the next proposals after 28 of 28 nonterminal batches, up from 14 of 28. Each task completed 29 updates, including one terminal update with no later proposals. The frozen representation and update equations were preserved, and all rank, covariance, path, step-size and sampling checks passed. Nevertheless, the seed-0 mean of final best scores fell from 0.302617 to 0.280194, a change of −0.022423 rather than the predicted gain of at least 0.002. zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.443203 to 0.363235, deco_hop from 0.610746 to 0.603856, drd2_docking from 0.063511 to 0.029010, and median_2 from 0.208415 to 0.198819. sitagliptin_mpo improved from 0.187211 to 0.206051. Both runs used all 300 evaluations per task. Raw Gaussian decodes rose from 4,800 to 9,280 across the suite; recorded suite time rose from 43.68 to 97.64 seconds, including oracle and runtime variation.

molecular.headline: Rings are abundant, but polyenes, oversized hydrocarbons and repeated imine/sulfur chains crowd out coherent medicinal scaffolds.
molecular.overall_character: This report describes n-47deaf126449 against Parent n-bd0cbfe35fa3 using the supplied seed 0 trajectories. Each task contains 300 unique evaluated molecules, of which 290 were proposed by the optimizer; the common initial structures are distinguished from generated output below. The generated structures cover many ring topologies and functional groups, so the problem is not absence of rings or complete structural collapse. However, high-scoring subsets repeatedly occupy chemically restricted families: unsaturated nitrogen rings, imine/sulfur networks, very long hydrocarbon chains, or an aromatic methylenedioxy motif attached to complicated carbonyl-bearing rings. Ring closure is ubiquitous in the digest, whereas aromatic character varies substantially across tasks. These are SMILES-text occurrence rates, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring-quality measurements. A closure digit can represent an ordinary phenyl ring, a highly strained unsaturated small ring, or an enormous macrocycle. Synthetic plausibility is questionable overall: recognizable aryl, ether, amide and cyclic-carbonyl fragments coexist with repetitive conjugation, unusual closures, reactive carbonyl arrangements and polysulfides. Some isolated structures and supplied initial molecules look substantially more conventional. Drug likeness is weak overall, while structural diversity is broad across the observed output and more restricted within recurring high-score motifs. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0: no explicit tetrahedral stereochemical annotation was emitted, even in structures that could have multiple stereogenic centers. This does not mean all structures are achiral. Score associations below describe the supplied observations; they do not establish a receptor interaction, a synthetic route, or a unique missing objective feature.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized, strongly unsaturated structures combine phenyl or pyridyl rings with imines, enamines, ethers and assorted nonaromatic nitrogen rings. The optimizer SMILES have mean length 36.1 and maximum length 74, ring_closure_rate 0.9897 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.8069. The best molecule, evaluation 281, connects a methoxyvinyl-substituted imine and pyridyl group to a phenyl-bearing unsaturated N-N ring. Evaluation 151 instead joins pyridyl and aryl-sulfoxide groups through a cyclobutadiene-like ring; evaluation 118 contains a cyclopropene and an unsaturated lactam. These are chemically very different arrangements despite neighboring high scores. The later trajectory favors carbonyl-poor imine/enamine and N-N ring structures, whereas the Parent retains more carbonyl-containing chains and rings. The common initial molecule at evaluation 9 is a much more conventional trimethoxyindole carboxamide with a fluorophenyl substituent; it was supplied, not generated.
liabilities: The cyclobutadiene-like ring at evaluation 151 and cyclopropene at evaluation 118 raise substantial ring-strain and synthesis concerns; ring-rich strings are not evidence of comfortable ring geometry.
Extended polyenes, enol ethers and imine/N-N arrangements create stability and isomerism questions. Alkene geometry and any tetrahedral stereochemistry are unspecified.
Large aromatic or unsaturated assemblies also appear among the lowest scores, so aromaticity alone is not a useful chemical quality argument.
missing_features: Reliable coverage of conventional aryl/heterocyclic frameworks with stable, deliberately placed polar functions is missing from the high-score series. The supplied indole carboxamide and the Parent best demonstrate relevant combinations, while the Child frequently substitutes imine/enamine networks and unusual ring closures.

There is no clear series that preserves a useful ring framework while separately exploring ordinary amide, ether and ring-nitrogen placement. The examples do not identify an additional unique objective-required substructure.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best generated score is 0.36323515471605416 at evaluation 281; evaluation 151 scores 0.3558775619487993 and the supplied indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. In contrast, the extended acyclic carbonate/amide polyene at evaluation 52 scores 7.550462063881703e-14, and the simple methoxypyridine carboxylic acid at evaluation 100 scores 2.188179510572902e-09. Thus neither making molecules smaller nor merely adding an aromatic nitrogen or carbonyl is sufficient. The higher examples support an association with a bounded aryl/heterocycle framework carrying distributed nitrogen and oxygen functions, but do not isolate a necessary group. The Parent maximum, 0.44320263021395917, belongs to an aryl nitrogen-ring structure that also retains a carboxamide and methoxyvinyl substituent. The Child does not reproduce that exact combination among its best examples. Its final hydrocarbon ring structure at evaluation 299 scores only 0.009441452624714554 despite retaining ring and aromatic syntax. The observed differences do not show that the unusual small rings themselves are beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The output is large, heavily unsaturated and usually aromatic, with nitrogen-rich heterocycles and increasingly repetitive imine, hydrazone, thioether and polysulfide connections. Mean SMILES length is 58.7, maximum length 98, ring_closure_rate 1.0 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9103. Evaluation 233, the best example, has a brominated conjugated ring framework, an enal substituent and an extended aza/sulfur ring network. Evaluation 146 expands a polyaza aromatic/imine framework around an enal. Evaluation 283 and the final evaluation 299 combine aza-aromatic and phenyl or thienyl rings with conspicuous sulfur chains and imine linkers. The whole trajectory confirms a shift from carbonyl-rich sulfone/lactam structures toward these repetitive nitrogen/sulfur arrangements. The Parent has more recognizable aryl amide, ester and ketone connections, although it too produces oversized and unusual conjugated structures.
liabilities: Repeated imines and hydrazones raise hydrolytic stability and configurational ambiguity concerns, and multiple sulfur-sulfur bonds introduce redox-sensitive connections.
Conjugated aldehydes occur in several best molecules, adding electrophilic functionality rather than demonstrating a benign medicinal series.
Extended aza/sulfur annulations and chains have questionable synthetic accessibility and substantial uncertainty in their preferred geometry and chemical stability.
missing_features: A comparably effective high-score family with bounded heterocycle/linker size and predominantly ordinary stable connections is not established in the Child. The Parent provides a more recognizable aryl-amide/ester counterexample to the apparent need for repeat expansion.

The output does not cleanly separate useful nitrogen-rich ring connectivity from redundant imine or sulfur repetition. The observed scores alone do not reveal a unique required decoration or scaffold arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 233 scores 0.6038558964255558 and evaluation 146 scores 0.5954516704042321. The sulfone-containing lactam/polyene at evaluation 64 scores 0.27028397565922924, and the aryl sulfone/amide/ester at evaluation 61 scores 0.27106627775076975. Within this output, aza-aromatic/imine connectivity, often accompanied by an enal and reduced sulfur linkers, occurs in the higher-score region; ordinary carbonyl or sulfone groups are not sufficient. Those features co-vary, so their individual contributions cannot be separated. The final polysulfide-rich evaluation 299 still scores 0.5919117647058824. The Parent best scores 0.6107459743674006 and combines a halogenated aryl amide, an alpha-keto ester and an aza-aromatic ring system without the Child high examples' extensive sulfur chains. This is evidence that the repetitive sulfur chemistry is not necessary to reach the observed score region, not proof that any particular replacement improves the score.

per_task.generated_character: This trajectory is dominated by very large aliphatic structures: long methylene chains, huge carbocyclic or heterocyclic loops, and occasional phenyl rings, ethers, acetals, alcohols, esters and lactones. Mean SMILES length is 78.4 and maximum length 147; ring_closure_rate is 0.9655, but aromatic_atom_rate is only 0.5. The best molecule at evaluation 210 combines a ring lactone and biaryl framework with extensive carbon chains and an aryl hydroxyethyl branch; it has no nitrogen. Evaluation 264 similarly retains a long aliphatic bridge inside an aromatic nitrogen/oxygen ring assembly. Evaluation 126 has long alkyl chains, aromatic rings and ester connections. By the final evaluations, 299 and 300 are almost entirely hydrocarbon, with a cyclohexyl ring and very long branched chains. The Parent also explores this large-chain chemistry, but its later output includes substantially more discrete aryl, ether, carbonyl and cyclic-amine arrangements.
liabilities: Very long, mostly nonpolar chains imply extreme flexibility and likely difficult aqueous handling; the final pure hydrocarbons offer almost no polar interaction diversity.
Precisely assembling enormous macrocycles and long chains with scattered acetals, alkenes or esters would be demanding, without evidence here of a useful defined conformation.
The repeated near-identical scores do not distinguish these liabilities or justify interpreting continued molecular growth as improved chemistry.
missing_features: The higher Child examples lack a comparably differentiated arrangement of discrete rings, polar functions and a cyclic amine like that observed in the Parent high-score region; alkyl repetition dominates instead. This is a missing combination, not evidence that any single nitrogen group is required.

Bounded hydrophobic substituents and controlled polar spacing are poorly represented in the late output. A unique missing receptor-interaction feature cannot be inferred from the nearly flat score regime, especially because the supplied cyclic-amine molecule scores poorly.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Many chemically different large structures share the recorded score 0.02885837683273086, including final evaluation 300; the digest median is 0.028858. The best molecule reaches only 0.029009639868631948. The polar chlorinated amino/amide/polyol at evaluation 21 scores 0.006307806495142862, and the supplied methylpiperidine-containing aromatic amide/hydroxamate at evaluation 6 scores 0.0003786988088202195. Thus the local observations favor the large-chain region over these examples, but then provide very little discrimination among its structures. They do not show that basic amines or additional polarity alone help. The Parent maximum is 0.06351092410835005 for a large but more structured molecule containing an aryl-substituted cyclic amine, a spiro ring junction, ether, alcohol, ketone and fluorinated aromatic substituents. The Child best and final molecules fail to recover that coordinated chemistry. The plateau cannot be interpreted as evidence of successful binding or assigned a physical cause from the molecular trajectories alone.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-score molecules repeatedly carry a benzodioxole, an aromatic ring bearing a cyclic methylenedioxy group, attached to saturated or partly unsaturated carbonyl-rich rings. The optimizer mean SMILES length is 52.8 and maximum length 123, with ring_closure_rate 0.9862 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.8276. Evaluation 135, the best, attaches this aromatic acetal to a complicated bridged/fused polyketone core with an alkyl substituent. Evaluation 123 uses an expanded lactone/diketone ring, while evaluation 104 has a smaller bridged carbonyl-bearing carbocycle. Other high examples preserve the aromatic acetal while changing ring closures, unsaturation and ketone or lactam positions. The structures have a natural-product-like mixture of aromatic and saturated carbon frameworks, but their arbitrary ring complexity and absent stereochemical assignments make actual preparation questionable. They are more than simple aromatic chains, yet they do not form a clearly controlled stereochemical series.
liabilities: Multiple ring junctions and saturated substituted centers would make stereoisomer control and synthesis demanding, but explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry is absent.
Closely spaced ketones and repeated enolizable carbonyl patterns add tautomeric and reactivity questions.
Convergence of the high-score excerpt on a common aromatic motif limits useful scaffold diversity despite many distinct molecular identities.
missing_features: The high-score Child excerpt lacks the Parent's simple, readily interpretable biaryl/ether alternatives around the recurring aromatic acetal. It does not show that complex bridged polyketones are necessary.

Controlled exploration of modest substituent and linker changes around the shared aromatic motif is limited relative to wholesale changes in the surrounding ring skeleton. No further unique objective-required motif can be recovered confidently from these examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best score is 0.19881918238645052 at evaluation 135; evaluations 123 and 104 score 0.19224322082161796 and 0.1896283315055771. The acyclic branched hydroxy-polyene at evaluation 290 scores 0.01355192713636236, and the small branched aldehyde at evaluation 115 scores 0.031250953717974365. The recurring aromatic methylenedioxy group with an attached ring framework is the clearest positive structural association. Ring complexity alone is not sufficient: the final dense polycycle at evaluation 299 lacks that recognizable aromatic motif and scores 0.10541990435198914, while evaluation 300 retains it and scores 0.17581973378636775. The Parent best is a much simpler ethoxy-substituted biaryl benzodioxole at 0.2084153270620087. The Child preserves the same useful aromatic motif but surrounds it with more elaborate carbonyl-bearing rings. These observations do not establish a reward for the added cage complexity or a requirement for its exact ketone pattern.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized, partially unsaturated nitrogen/oxygen rings carry ketones, amides, lactones, aldehydes, phenols or enols; aromatic rings are less prevalent than in most other task outputs. Mean SMILES length is 36.9 and maximum length 84, ring_closure_rate 0.9138 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.3517. Evaluation 280, the best, combines a phenolic aromatic ring, an unsaturated nitrogen ring framework and an amino-ketone side chain. Evaluation 88 combines an unsaturated nitrogen ring with a brominated formylphenyl group and a conjugated N-formyl amide. Evaluation 213 is an unsaturated nitrogen-containing macrocyclic lactone with formyl and enolic functions. Formal charge syntax is relatively frequent: charged_rate 0.2276, with cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1103. Evaluation 83 illustrates a formally charged cumulated nitrogen/oxygen arrangement alongside an amide and brominated unsaturated nitrogen ring. These counters do not establish the physical protonation or stability of those species.
liabilities: Several high examples contain aldehydes, conjugated carbonyls or enol/imine arrangements that raise stability and reactivity concerns.

Formally charged cumulated nitrogen/oxygen groups and other unusual nitrogen bonding appear among usable-score molecules, so the observed score does not itself screen out chemically questionable functionality.

Unsaturated macrocycles, uncommon fused ring closures and unspecified stereochemistry make the apparent molecular graphs more definite than their real chemical identities and accessible conformations.
missing_features: A stable, systematically varied family that retains the favorable size and nitrogen/oxygen balance is not established. Amino-carbonyl, hydroxylated imine and lactone arrangements appear as disparate examples rather than an interpretable series of conventional heterocycles.

Defined saturation and stereochemical arrangements around the substituted ring systems are absent. Their potential usefulness is a chemistry capability gap; these trajectories do not demonstrate a stereochemical score preference or justify prescribing a specific target-like motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best scores are 0.20605067334417151 at evaluation 280, 0.20209403173605398 at evaluation 88 and 0.1982617738654109 at evaluation 213, while the digest median is 0.000488. The larger aromatic amide/nitro/polyene assembly at evaluation 11 scores 1.0124110977439176e-51. Moderate size and a mixed nitrogen/oxygen cyclic framework recur among the higher examples, but they are not sufficient: the compact nitrogen/carbonyl polycycle at evaluation 261 scores 2.319795379947775e-43. Nor is avoiding formal charge a universal separator, because evaluation 83 scores 0.1775105772728547. The Parent best at 0.18721053870914972 instead combines a hydroxylated cyclic imine, primary amine and cyanophenyl substituent. The Child best changes the functional-group combination while retaining a bounded nitrogen/oxygen framework. The score differences do not identify one necessary halogen, amine type, carbonyl arrangement or hidden reference scaffold. The final molecules remain chemically mixed, with evaluation 300 at 0.07900628938932339.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring_closure_rate reaches 1.0, yet the cited high-score molecules include cyclobutadiene-like and cyclopropene rings, extended unsaturated macrocycles and complicated bridged polyketones. The Parent also supplies a simpler aromatic ether/acetal framework at 0.2084153270620087, so elaborate closures are not a demonstrated prerequisite for useful scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring closure does not translate into reliable conventional ring geometry or controlled unsaturation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs support for ordinary aromatic, saturated and partly saturated ring frameworks with chemically sensible closure geometry, while allowing controlled substitution and fusion. Ring presence and parsable valence alone do not establish that capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One full trajectory repeatedly emits very long hydrocarbon chains at the identical recorded score 0.02885837683273086 and ends with almost pure hydrocarbons. Another high-score excerpt contains long alternating imine sequences and sulfur chains, including a final polysulfide-rich molecule at 0.5919117647058824. These are repeated structural patterns, not merely long SMILES caused by ordinary ring notation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably bound molecular extent or repeated backbone and linker units.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded, diverse chain and linker architectures and distinct functional-group placements without requiring extension of the same carbon, imine or sulfur unit. Preserve access to shorter alternatives so observed feedback can distinguish chemistry beyond repeat length.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145, and a Parent high example combines a cyclic amine, ether, alcohol and ketone at 0.06351092410835005. Generated high-score excerpts instead often emphasize carbonyl-poor imine/N-N rings, sulfur networks or almost entirely hydrocarbon structures. The poor score of a supplied methylpiperidine-containing molecule also shows that simply inserting an amine is not sufficient.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ordinary polar functions are available but are not reliably retained together in balanced ring-based structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to varied amide, ether, alcohol and amine contexts with controlled hydrophobic and polar spacing. The needed capability is coherent combinations and independent variation of those functions, rather than a mandatory group for any hidden objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited aromatic methylenedioxy examples retain the same local motif while cycling through bridged polyketones, expanded lactones and unsaturated fused systems. Elsewhere related aza-aromatic fragments are embedded in progressively different imine and sulfur networks. The digest reports 300 unique molecules per task, but distinct identities do not establish broad exploration of simple alternatives around a useful motif.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful motif diversity is often expressed through large changes in surrounding topology instead of modest, interpretable chemical variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support families that preserve a coherent ring framework while varying attachment position, linker size, saturation and ordinary polar substituents. This would expose more interpretable chemical alternatives without encoding the identity of the objective or asserting that one recurring motif is universally useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied optimizer digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited bridged carbonyl-rich structures, substituted lactones and partially saturated ring junctions nevertheless contain potential stereogenic arrangements. Their written molecular identities therefore leave chemically relevant configurations unresolved.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry is absent even where the generated ring frameworks could require it.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to represent and preserve defined stereoisomers of substituted saturated and fused ring frameworks to explore that chemistry. This capability should be available independently of objective identity; the present trajectories do not establish that a particular stereoisomer would score better.

method_name: CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder
method_thesis: Anchor the optimizer in CMA-ES: sample a multivariate Gaussian, rank evaluated samples, move its mean by weighted recombination, and adapt covariance and step size using selected displacements and cumulative evolution paths. [Hansen, Sections 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1604.00772v2) describes this mechanism. For the molecular transfer, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder. Each objective starts with fresh Gaussian and path state. Encodings of high-scoring supplied molecules may initialize geometric search locations, but their scores must not be assigned to nonidentical reconstructions. Generate latent samples, decode them into new molecules, and attach accepted oracle feedback to the exact latent sample that produced each submitted structure. Assemble scored generations while respecting the evaluator-announced batching, then update the Gaussian from descending observed-score ranks. Reject invalid or duplicate structures locally and continue de novo decoding. The corpus trains a generator and never supplies a ranked molecular library. The hypothesis is that learning correlated latent displacements directly from successful generations can uncover improving combinations without first estimating an objective surrogate, increasing the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Useful decoder support and covariance adaptation within scarce feedback are empirical prerequisites; continuous-domain performance is not evidence that decoded molecular landscapes will behave similarly.
